name: AR-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -20 point partisan lean
Incumbent Bruce Westerman has a massive financial advantage ($4.7M on hand vs. under $1,000)
Challenger James Russell has raised only about $5,900, indicating a minimal campaign
Prediction markets price Westerman at roughly 97% to win
model.rationale: This is a deeply Republican district where Westerman, a well-funded incumbent, faces a challenger who has raised almost no money. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Republican win with little evidence to suggest otherwise.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending or unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only plausible route to a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bruce Westerman seeks another term in a southern Arkansas district that leans about twenty points toward Republicans. He has built a large war chest of roughly $4.7 million, while Democratic challenger James Russell has raised under six thousand dollars and holds less than a thousand on hand, signaling a campaign with minimal resources.

No public polling or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Westerman about a 97 percent chance of winning. The fundamentals, the money gap, and the district's partisan makeup all align on a comfortable Republican victory, with the Democratic challenger facing steep structural odds.
